title: Experimental Observation of Dynamical Phase Transitions in a Dephased Photonic Quantum Walk
authors: Xiaojian Huang, Lei Xiao, Bingzi Huo, Xiaowei Wang, Stefano Longhi, Peng Xue
abstract: Dynamical phase transitions in open quantum systems govern how non-equilibrium states relax toward a stationary state. We study these transitions experimentally using a discrete-time photonic quantum walk on a three-node graph. A tunable synthetic gauge flux and calibrated dephasing allow us to control time-reversal symmetry and the detailed balance properties of the effective Markovian dynamics. With detailed balance, we observe a first-order dynamical phase transition marked by a crossing of real Liouvillian eigenvalues. When detailed balance is broken, we observe a second-order dynamical phase transition at an exceptional point where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce. By progressively reducing the dephasing strength, we track the crossover toward the quantum-coherent regime and determine that the transitions persist down to a finite threshold. Our results link Liouvillian spectral topology to relaxation criticality and demonstrate a controllable platform for engineered dissipative dynamics.
summary: The research experimentally explores dynamical phase transitions in open quantum systems using a photonic quantum walk. By controlling dephasing and synthetic magnetic flux, the authors successfully observe both first-order (FOPT) and second-order (SOPT) transitions. This work establishes a programmable platform for engineering dissipative dynamics by linking spectral properties to relaxation criticality.
main_problem: The study investigates dynamical phase transitions (DPTs) in open quantum systems, which govern how non-equilibrium states relax toward a stationary state.
main_result: The authors experimentally demonstrated both first-order (FOPT) and second-order (SOPT) DPTs by controlling dephasing strength and synthetic gauge flux in a photonic quantum walk platform.
method: The dynamics are analyzed by reconstructing the Floquet-Liouvillian superoperator from single-photon measurements to extract eigenvalues, which diagnose the nature of the phase transition via crossings or coalescence at exceptional points.
model_or_system: The system is a discrete-time photonic quantum walk (OQW) implemented on a three-node graph using a single-photon interferometric network. The dynamics are governed by a master equation incorporating tunable dephasing ($q$) and synthetic gauge flux ($\phi$).
key_observables: Eigenvalue crossings (for FOPT), coalescence of eigenvalues/eigenvectors at Exceptional Points (EPs) (for SOPT), and order parameters like the eigenvalue splitting $\Delta\lambda$ and eigenmode overlap $g$.
important_parameters: Dephasing strength ($q$), synthetic gauge flux ($\phi$), and the evolution parameter ($ eta$). The transitions are shown to persist down to a finite threshold.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on reconstructing the transition matrix from measured probabilities and assumes that the observed spectral features accurately map onto theoretical predictions for DPTs.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the FOPT in the fully dephased limit ($\phi=0$) showing eigenvalue crossings, and the SOPT in the broken TRS regime ($\phi=\pi/3$) showing EP signatures. Scaling laws near EPs are also presented.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework of DPTs in open systems using a photonic OQW model. It then details experimental measurements to diagnose FOPT (TRS-preserving) and SOPT (TRS-breaking), demonstrating control over these transitions by tuning dephasing and flux, and confirming scaling laws near EPs.
why_interesting: This work provides an unprecedentedly controllable platform—using photonics—to experimentally map out the rich phase diagram of dissipative quantum dynamics, linking spectral topology directly to relaxation criticality in a highly tunable manner.

FIG. 2. Second-order dynamical phase transition in the fully dephased benchmark (q = 1) with broken TRS (ϕ = π/3). (a),(b) Measured populations Pi(s) at β = 0.70 < βc and β = 1.20 > βc, showing monotonic and damped-oscillatory relaxation. (c),(d) Real and imaginary components of the two non-stationary right eigenmodes r(1) and r(2) of Q (solid bars: experiment with error bars; open rectangles: theory). (e) Re[λk] versus β, showing coalescence of the two non- stationary exponents at βc. (f) Im[λk], showing the emer- gence of a complex-conjugate pair for β > βc.

FIG. 3. Quantum-regime validation in the OQW. Experimentally measured Re[λ1,2] (top row) and eigenvector overlap g (bottom row) versus β at representative dephasing strengths. (a),(b) TRS case (ϕ = 0) at q = 0.8: a real-eigenvalue crossing signals an FOPT while g < 1 confirms distinct eigenmodes. (c),(d) Same as (a),(b) but for q = 0.5. (e),(f) Broken-TRS case (ϕ = π/3) at q = 0.8: eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce at an EP, yielding an SOPT with g →1. (g),(h) Same as (e),(f) but for q = 0.5. Vertical dashed lines indicate βc. Solid curves are theoretical predictions; symbols are experimental data with photon-counting error bars.

FIG. 4. Experimental schematic. Each discrete-time step of the OQW consists of a coherent unitary operation U followed by a dephasing channel. Beam displacers map the three path modes to spatially separated ports, which are detected by APDs to yield node-resolved counts. Thin outlined boxes indicate 45◦HWPs used for mode readdressing between the two BDs. Dashed ellipses mark QHQ sets implementing the two-mode unitaries Ui,j in the decomposition of U. The optical synthesis of the full 3 × 3 step unitary U is shown in the solid box.

FIG. 6. Complementary scans deeper into the quantum regime. Same observables as Fig. 3, shown for q = 0.6 and 0.1. (a),(b) TRS case (ϕ = 0) at q = 0.6: the real-eigenvalue crossing persists (FOPT) and g remains below unity. (c),(d) TRS case at q = 0.1: no resolvable spectral crossing is observed and g shows no critical feature, indicating suppressed criticality. (e),(f) Broken-TRS case (ϕ = π/3) at q = 0.6: the EP-driven SOPT remains visible through simultaneous eigenvalue and eigenvector coalescence (g →1). (g),(h) Broken-TRS case at q = 0.1: the EP signature and the corresponding peak in g are washed out. Vertical dashed lines indicate βc where a critical point is identifiable.
